note: Phase 7 planned execution manifest for reviewer-facing history, first-class record delete or restore, rollback, retained history, and destructive-operation lock precedence. Sprint 0 creates selectable placeholders only; product behavior remains unimplemented until later Phase 7 sprints.

ledger.title: Phase 7 Coverage Ledger
notes: Phase 7 remains registered as planned. This manifest records ownership and placeholder evidence locations before feature work, but public phase wrappers must not execute Phase 7 rows until the registry status is intentionally activated.

`AC-184` and `AC-185` appear in the Phase 7 guide row `U-7-01`, but the guide coverage index assigns those ACs to Phase 8. Sprint 0 records them as ambiguous support references, not completed Phase 7 claims.
Typed tag rollback language is treated as an owner-decision dependency; Phase 7 placeholders must not claim Phase 8 typed tag creation or mutation behavior.
authoritative_execution: `backend-store` will carry authoritative `U-7-*` route and store-domain rows through manifest-owned service-backed Go selection after Phase 7 activation.

`backend-integration` will carry authoritative `I-7-*` real-runtime rows for source state, projections, history rows, collaboration events, pagination, restart, and incident-closure behavior after Phase 7 activation.
`browser-e2e-webserver-backed` will carry authoritative `E-7-*` browser-functional rows through manifest-entry shards under `browser_functional` after Phase 7 activation.
`frontend-unit` may carry supplemental component scaffolding for the reviewer history surface, but frontend-unit rows do not replace authoritative browser `E-7-*` evidence.
support_execution_extras: Phase 3 through Phase 6 mutation, projection, idempotency, conflict, evidence, merge, and collaboration tests remain carryover support only and must not claim Phase 7 identifiers.
When Phase 7 activates, missing duration baselines must be refreshed from clean successful service-backed and browser evidence rather than hidden behind fallback weights.
shared_harness: | Planned manifest ownership | `tools/phase7_test_map.json` records every authoritative guide row before product behavior exists. |
| Generated ledger | `docs/testing/phase7_coverage_ledger.md` is generated from this manifest and must not be hand-edited. |
| Schedule boundary | Phase 7 remains planned, so generated schedules must not add Phase 7 execution work until `tools/phase_registry.json` explicitly activates the phase. |
support_only: `internal/modules/timeline`, `internal/modules/entities`, `internal/modules/evidence`, `internal/modules/workbook`, and `internal/modules/collaboration` Phase 3 through Phase 6 tests provide substrate support only.
`apps/web/src/WorkbookShell.phase7.test.tsx` is supplemental UI scaffolding for future reviewer-history controls and must not replace authoritative `E-7-*` browser rows.
Existing browser specs under `apps/web/e2e/phase4*`, `phase5*`, and `phase6*` remain prior-phase evidence and are forbidden from claiming Phase 7 IDs.

unit.claim: `GET /api/v1/records/{record_id}/history` returns the Phase 7 record-scoped history envelope with newest-first deterministic items, deleted-row tombstone `row_version`, and canonical `available_rollback_actions[]` ordering.
unit.out_of_scope: `AC-184` and `AC-185` remain ambiguous Phase 8-assigned support references until an owner decision resolves the guide drift.
unit.template_clone_reason: Phase 7 history route coverage will exercise persisted change sets, mutation entries, record revisions, records, and tombstone state through the runtime-backed store harness.

unit.claim: `history_entry_ref` is present only for a logical history item that maps to exactly one reversible mutation target, stays opaque to clients, and remains stable across repeated reads.
unit.out_of_scope: Whole-change-set and whole-row rollback execution are covered by rollback rows.
unit.template_clone_reason: Selector stability coverage needs durable persisted history materialization rather than in-memory-only helpers.

unit.claim: First-class record soft-delete requires current `row_version`, respects role gates, and returns route-owned failures including `record_deleted_use_restore`, `record_not_deleted`, and applicable `record_locked` behavior.
unit.out_of_scope: Restore append-only consequences and destructive lock precedence are separate Phase 7 rows.
unit.template_clone_reason: Soft-delete route coverage requires persisted record envelope state and route-scoped idempotency.

unit.claim: Restore requires the current tombstone `row_version`, respects role gates, returns the record to active state, and never mutates prior history rows in place.
unit.out_of_scope: Browser-visible delete and restore collaboration behavior is covered by `E-7-03`.
unit.template_clone_reason: Restore route coverage needs durable tombstone concurrency and append-only history state.

unit.claim: Rollback accepts only `history_entry`, `change_set`, and `row_restore` targets and creates a new `change_set` with `source='rollback'` rather than mutating prior history.
unit.out_of_scope: Typed tag creation or mutation semantics remain outside Sprint 0 and must not be claimed until an owner decision pulls them into Phase 7.
unit.template_clone_reason: Rollback selector coverage requires persisted change sets, mutation entries, and record revisions.

unit.claim: Restore, rollback, and merge use shared destructive-operation lock precedence, fail fast before stale-precondition evaluation, and replay ordinary downstream route errors after lock release.
unit.out_of_scope: Ordinary soft-delete and ordinary patch stay outside the destructive-operation family.
unit.template_clone_reason: Lock precedence coverage needs real transaction-scoped persisted record locks.

unit.claim: Retained history for extant records remains fully paginatable and preserves issued `history_entry_ref` values across incident closure, delete or restore cycles, rollback, and restart.
unit.out_of_scope: The current profile defines no public history-purge route or retention-horizon setting for extant incidents.
unit.template_clone_reason: Retained-history coverage needs durable committed state across lifecycle transitions and restart boundaries.

unit.title: Phase 7 U-7-FE-01 keeps reviewer history controls as planned UI support
unit.claim: Supplemental component coverage anchors future reviewer-history controls to server-provided selectors and actions.
unit.out_of_scope: Authoritative reviewer workflows remain browser `E-7-*` rows.

integration.claim: Delete, restore, and rollback update source rows, projections, history rows, and emitted collaboration events atomically.
integration.out_of_scope: Single-route request-shape validation remains unit or store-domain evidence.
integration.template_clone_reason: Atomic consequence coverage requires real runtime state across source tables, projections, history tables, and collaboration publication.

integration.claim: History pagination remains bound to `record_id`, rejects cross-record cursor replay, and preserves deterministic item ordering across pages.
integration.out_of_scope: General pagination registry behavior remains existing platform support evidence.
integration.template_clone_reason: Record-bound cursor coverage requires persisted multi-record history and real HTTP cursor handling.

integration.claim: A stale restore or rollback precondition fails closed and never mutates current row state.
integration.out_of_scope: Lock acquisition precedence is covered by `U-7-06`.
integration.template_clone_reason: Stale-precondition coverage requires committed current state and HTTP rollback or restore behavior.

integration.claim: History for an extant record remains fully paginatable and stable across service restart, incident closure, delete or restore, and rollback, with prior `history_entry_ref` values preserved.
integration.out_of_scope: Incident portability selector preservation across deployments is outside Phase 7.
integration.template_clone_reason: Restart and closure coverage requires durable runtime-backed history evidence.

e2e.title: E-7-01 opens row history from the workbook surface with legal rollback actions
e2e.claim: A reviewer opens row history from the workbook surface and sees actor, timestamp, operation, diff summary, and server-provided legal rollback actions.
e2e.out_of_scope: History route envelope construction remains backend evidence.

e2e.title: E-7-02 rolls back one mistaken mutation without reverting later unrelated edits
e2e.claim: A reviewer rolls back one mistaken link, tag, mention resolution, or evidence association without reverting later unrelated edits on the same row.
e2e.out_of_scope: Typed tag mutation semantics remain owner-decision dependent and must not be inferred from this placeholder.

e2e.title: E-7-03 soft-deletes and restores a row with tombstone concurrency
e2e.claim: A reviewer soft-deletes and restores a row using tombstone concurrency, while other clients observe `remove` on delete and `invalidate` on restore.
e2e.out_of_scope: Low-level destructive lock precedence remains backend evidence.

e2e.title: E-7-04 whole-row restore appends a new attributed revision
e2e.claim: Whole-row restore creates a new attributed revision and moves the visible row back to the selected historical snapshot without erasing prior history.
e2e.out_of_scope: Whole-change-set rollback internals remain backend evidence.
